explanation: Baking soda needs an acid, such as buttermilk or lemon juice, to react. Baking powder carries its own dry acid, so it works with water alone.

claims.text: Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) and baking powder release carbon dioxide gas, which makes cakes rise.
Baking soda and baking powder do not leaven cakes by releasing oxygen, nitrogen or hydrogen.
Baking soda needs an acidic ingredient, such as buttermilk or lemon juice, to release carbon dioxide.
Baking powder contains baking soda plus a dry acid, so it releases carbon dioxide when moistened.
